claims.text: Guardian (11 Sep 2013), memorandum agreed in principle March 2009: NSA shares raw unfiltered phone/internet data with Israel including US citizens' communications; NSA not required to remove US persons' data; no limits on Israel's use reported; Israel must 'destroy upon recognition' communications of US government officials (executive, Congress, federal courts); NSA: handled under procedures 'designed to protect privacy rights'.

NSA 2013 document: 'far-reaching technical and analytic relationship' with ISNU (Unit 8200), 'a dedicated communications line between NSA and ISNU [that] supports the exchange of raw material'; Israel 'enjoys the benefits of expanded geographic access' and 'gains controlled access to advanced U.S. technology and equipment'; Israeli priorities include 'Palestinian terrorism'. 2003–04 'Gladiator' receipts for $500,000 cash payments to Israeli officials, deal apparently never consummated.

NSA 2008 document (Intercept 2015): Israel 'also targets us'; a National Intelligence Estimate ranked Israel third most aggressive intelligence service against the US; 2013 budget document lists Israel among hostile intelligence services/cyber threats; Netanyahu's office (24 Mar 2015): 'The state of Israel does not conduct espionage against the United States or Israel's other allies.'

entries.topic: The 2009 raw-SIGINT memorandum and the balance of exchange

claims.text: Memorandum (as published by the Guardian): 'NSA routinely sends ISNU minimised and unminimised raw collection'; raw includes 'unevaluated and unminimized transcripts'; Israel may keep 'any files containing the identities of US persons' for up to a year, consulting an NSA liaison; must 'destroy upon recognition' communications to or from US government officials (executive, Congress, federal courts); NSA will 'regularly review a sample of files transferred to ISNU'; 'This agreement is not intended to create any legally enforceable rights' and is not a legally binding instrument; access limited to a 'strict need to know'.

Techdirt summary: NSA performs only 'a minimal pre-screen of random samples'; Israel may share with 'outside parties' with NSA written permission after stripping identifiers; 'The agreement places no legally binding limits on the use of the data by the Israelis.'

NSA statement (2013): US-person information 'is handled under procedures that are designed to protect privacy rights'; 'NSA cannot, however, use these relationships to circumvent US legal restrictions'; NSA declined to say whether the FISA court approved the agreement.

2007 NSA history 'History of the US – Israel Sigint Relationship, Post-1992': 'Balancing the Sigint exchange equally between US and Israeli needs has been a constant challenge'; 'In the last decade, it arguably tilted heavily in favor of Israeli security concerns.' A 2008 document quotes a senior NSA official: 'One of NSA's biggest threats is actually from friendly intelligence services, like Israel.' 2013 budget request lists Israel alongside Iran and China as a target for US cyber operations (via Washington Post).

Intercept 2019: during the 2006 Lebanon war ISNU relied heavily on NSA for tasking, warning, tactical ELINT and geolocation on Hezbollah; the NSA liaison called geolocation requests 'particularly problematic' because of NSA's prohibition on providing information usable in targeted killings; ISNU commander sought an exemption; ODNI brokered a framework; a 2007 NSA slide put ISNU at about 5,500 conscripts and 1,200 career officers.

entries.topic: What each side gets; Israel as counterintelligence threat; US collection on Israel

claims.text: NSA document (13 Apr 2013): 'NSA maintains a far-reaching technical and analytic relationship with the Israeli SIGINT National Unit', 'sharing information on access, intercept, targeting, language, analysis and reporting'; 'a dedicated communications line between NSA and ISNU [that] supports the exchange of raw material'; Israel gains 'expanded geographic access to world-class NSA cryptanalytic and SIGINT engineering expertise' and 'controlled access to advanced U.S. technology and equipment via accommodation buys and foreign military sales'; targets include North Africa, the Middle East, the Persian Gulf; Israeli priorities include 'Palestinian terrorism'. NSA spokesperson: cooperation 'mutually strengthens the security of both nations'.

NSA 2008 document: 'Israel also targets us'; 'A NIE ranked [Israel] as the third most aggressive intelligence service against the US'; the 2013 budget lists Israel among 'most threatening cyber-adversaries' and as a 'hostile' service; Netanyahu's office: 'The state of Israel does not conduct espionage against the United States or Israel's other allies.'
The Netanyahu denial followed a Wall Street Journal report (March 2015) that Israel spied on the US–Iran negotiations and passed material to members of Congress.

WSJ (29 Dec 2015): NSA kept intercepting Netanyahu's communications after Obama's January 2014 curbs on monitoring allied leaders, Netanyahu being kept off the protected list for a 'compelling national security purpose'; intercepts showed Israeli efforts to turn Congress against the Iran deal; a 2011 NSA directive requires destruction of intercepted communications between foreign targets and members of Congress unless the NSA director waives it for 'significant foreign intelligence'; NSC: no surveillance 'unless there is a specific and validated national security purpose'; Israeli embassy declined comment.

entries.topic: Unit 8200, the 2014 letter, alumni in US tech, Azure, and what US oversight can see

claims.text: 43 Unit 8200 reservists (10 officers) wrote to Netanyahu, Gantz and Kochavi (reported 12 Sep 2014): 'The intelligence gathered harms innocents and is used for political persecution'; 'Our conscience no longer permits us to serve this system'; a cosignatory said the task was 'not defense but ruling another people'.

Check Point founded 1993 by Gil Shwed, Shlomo Kramer and Marius Nacht; Shwed and Kramer served in Unit 8200; Nir Zuk, an 8200 alumnus and early Check Point employee, founded Palo Alto Networks; CyberArk CEO Udi Mokady and Cybereason's founders are described as 8200 alumni.

Wiz: Rappaport joined Unit 8200 after university; the founders met in the Talpiot programme; Microsoft bought their earlier company Adallom in 2015 for $320m and they led Microsoft's Cloud Security Group until 2020; Google completed its $32bn cash acquisition of Wiz on 11 Mar 2026.

Guardian/+972/Local Call (6 Aug 2025): Unit 8200 stored millions of intercepted Palestinian calls from Gaza and the West Bank on Azure in the Netherlands and Ireland ('a million calls an hour'); at least 11,500 terabytes by July 2025; sources said used to identify airstrike targets and justify arrests; Sariel met Nadella in 2021; Microsoft said it had 'no information' about surveillance of civilians; IDF: 'legally supervised agreements'.

Microsoft (Brad Smith, 25 Sep 2025): found 'evidence that supports elements of The Guardian's reporting', including IMOD consumption of Azure storage in the Netherlands and use of AI services; decided to 'cease and disable specified IMOD subscriptions'; 'We do not provide technology to facilitate mass surveillance of civilians'; Microsoft did not access customer content; an Israeli security official told AP there would be 'no damage to the operational capabilities'; Israel Hayom reported a shift reportedly to Amazon Web Services.

NSM-20 report (10 May 2024): 'Israel has not shared complete information to verify whether U.S. defense articles were specifically used'; 'difficult to assess or reach conclusive findings on individual incidents' given lack of US personnel on the ground; 'reasonable to assess' US weapons were used in instances inconsistent with IHL obligations.
Pentagon (Brig. Gen. Pat Ryder, Nov 2023): 'In support of hostage recovery efforts, the U.S. is conducting unarmed [UAV] flights over Gaza'; MQ-9s per flight-tracking data.

The terms of US intelligence-sharing agreements and safeguards are not public; ACLU lists unilateral data-sharing agreements with Israel, Germany and Saudi Arabia; FBI rules for sharing s.702 data are fully redacted; the most recent public UKUSA text dates from 1955 and FOIA requests for current terms had not produced records.
